retail.cancellation_matching: an original line is dropped when a later cancellation has the same customer, StockCode and quantity (the latest earlier match); this removes cancelled bulk orders such as 74,215 units of 23166 on 18 Jan 2011
retail.description: Series start at each product's first week with a sale and are zero-filled to the last full week.

grid.target: ND (national demand, MW): transmission demand excluding station load, pumping and exports
grid.temperature_note: Daily GB average temperature outturn (BMRS TEMP), repeated over the 48 half-hours of its local day. It is an actual, not a forecast: an oracle covariate.
grid.neso_note: NESO notes data issues on its Demand Data Update for 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-13 (under review on 2026-10-20); those days are used as published.

conventions.mase: MAE of the median over the mean absolute seasonal difference of the in-sample history; period 1 for weekly retail, 48 for half-hourly grid (GIFT-Eval / GluonTS seasonality). Sweep tasks scale every truncation by the same full history.
conventions.wql: mean over levels 0.1..0.9 of 2 * sum(pinball loss) / sum(|y|) (GIFT-Eval CRPS proxy). wql_pooled sums over every window of a task, as GIFT-Eval does per dataset.
conventions.relative: relative_mase_geomean: geometric mean over windows of model MASE / seasonal-naive MASE, skipping pairs where either is zero; CI from a series-level bootstrap. relative_wql_pooled: pooled WQL over pooled seasonal-naive WQL.
point_only_models: have nine identical quantiles: their WQL is the point forecast's, and coverage and the p90 order are not reported
conventions.newsvendor: order each week at the 90th-percentile forecast (optimal only if a unit short costs 9x a unit left over); units short and units left over, summed over all windows
conventions.retail_clip: every retail quantile clipped at zero, for every contender
